chapter: Playing in New Orleans and influences
title: Playing Arthur Ogle's funeral with a pickup band
summary: A pickup Eureka band played the drummer's funeral and then jammed at the Caledonia Inn.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: I stuck with him from nine till four. And then recently I played Arthur Ogle's Funeral. You know, he, um, he's an old drummer of the Eureka. He's on the Pax record and he had both his legs amputated before I even got to town. He died about a month ago and I played, uh, there was no money involved in it and she asked me to play. Uh, Percy couldn't make it. And, uh, Bokaj couldn't, Bokaj wasn't there and Jim Crow couldn't make it. He was playing with the Eureka at that time. He, somebody had to fix his TV set or something. So he had to stay at home and Red Clark couldn't make it. And the drummer they couldn't get in touch with. So he was just about a pickup band. Paul Barberin played bass drum. They got him at the last minute. And Kid Howard joined us halfway through. The funeral was in the church right opposite the bar where Howard drinks. Right there. You know where it is on, uh, Liberty, very close to the Civic Auditorium where Jim Robinson lives and Sonny Henry lives there too. Howard lives there. They all live just on that corner.
I don't know. Sonny lives downtown, I think.

That's right. By the Civic Auditorium. Oh yeah, yeah. It's on, it's Liberty is it or someone or something. And anyway, I don't know. On Marais. St. Philip. Yeah, somewhere around Marais and St. Philip. Or Liberty and St. Philip.
So close to the, uh. Rampart. Caledonia. That's right. Well now. Is that the bar?

Yeah, that's not the bar where they drink, but that's where we finished up. We played, uh, it was a very short funeral and played a couple of, uh, spirituals, not dirges. I can't play dirges. I can play spiritual slowly. And, uh, then we marched back to the Caledonia Inn and then we all went in there and played, oh, for about an hour. Uh huh. Just playing, you know, just for kicks, because somehow nobody was getting paid so nobody seemed to care. And all the people at the Eureka who were sort of in command, they were the ones that, uh, couldn't make it. So, nobody seemed to mind. That was very pleasant.
That's the only funeral I've ever played. 된 stuff with
